missed.text: For photometric measurements of a retro-reflective device of Class IA or IB, the illuminating surface itself shall be limited to 100 cm2 though the surfaces of the retro-reflecting optical units need not necessarily attain this area.

When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI values for red retro-reflectors shall be equal to or greater than those in Table 3, expressed in millicandelas per lux, for the angles of divergence and illumination shown.
The trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous flux shall be within the limits for the night-time colours red, amber or white as specified in UN Regulation No. 48.

The lighting and light-signalling devices shall be so fitted that under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations to which the lighting and light-signalling devices may be subjected, the lighting and light-signalling devices enable the vehicle to comply with the requirements of this Regulation.

The lighting and light-signalling devices shall prevent the lamps from being inadvertently maladjusted under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations to which the lighting and light-signalling devices may be subjected.

For all light-signalling devices, including those mounted on the side panels, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the bearing plane of the vehicle on the road, with a tolerance of ±3° allowed in each direction.

For all light-signalling devices other than side retro-reflectors and side-marker lamps, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ±3° allowed in each direction.
For all light-signalling devices, including those mounted on the side panels, any specific instructions as regards fitting laid down by the manufacturer shall be complied with.
The lamps shall have substantially identical photometric characteristics, except that this shall not apply to a matched pair of a function and/or an AFS.

When a front or rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with one or more other function(s) which can be switched ON together with them, and the reciprocally incorporated function(s) and the front or rear position lamps are switched ON, the front or rear position lamp shall fulfill the requirements regarding colour of each of these other functions.

The electrical connections shall be such that the front and rear position lamps, the end-outline marker lamps, if they exist, the side-marker lamps, if they exist, and the rear registration plate lamp can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.

Rear position lamps, rear direction-indicator lamps and rear retro-reflectors (triangular or not) may be installed on movable components only if the conditions of paragraph 5.18.1. or 5.18.2. are met.

The reversing lamp shall be not less than 250 mm and not more than 1,200 mm above the ground, except that for category N2G, N3G, M2G, M3G (off-road) vehicles the maximum height may be increased to 1,400 mm.
All categories of vehicles shall be equipped with two S1 or S2 category devices and one S3 or S4 category device.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles, for S1 or S2 categories devices, the point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
Where the optional lamps are installed, the optional lamps shall be positioned at a height compatible with the requirements of the width and the symmetry of the lamps.

Where optional lamps are installed, the optional lamps shall be positioned at a vertical distance as large as the shape of the bodywork makes it possible, but not less than 600 mm above the mandatory lamps.

The vertical angle of geometric visibility for S1 or S2 categories devices shall be 15° above and below the horizontal, except that (a) where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°; (b) where an optional lamp is mounted above 2,100 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above) the upward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.

Where optional rear position lamps are installed, the optional rear position lamps shall be placed at a height compatible with the applicable requirements of paragraph 6.10.4.1. and the symmetry of the lamps.

Where optional rear position lamps are installed, the optional rear position lamps shall be placed at a vertical distance as large as the shape of the bodywork makes it possible, but not less than 600 mm above the mandatory lamps.

Where an optional lamp is mounted above 2,100 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1. above), the lamp shall have a vertical angle of 15° above and below the horizontal, except that the upward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.

Where a rear side-marker lamp is installed on the vehicle, for M1 and N1 category vehicles, as an alternative to paragraph 6.10.5.1., at the discretion of the manufacturer or his duly accredited representative, the rear position lamp shall have a horizontal angle of geometric visibility of 45° outwards to 45° inwards; however, where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

Where a rear side-marker lamp is installed on the vehicle, for M1 and N1 category vehicles, as an alternative to paragraph 6.10.5.1., at the discretion of the manufacturer or his duly accredited representative, the rear position lamp shall have a vertical angle of geometric visibility of 15° above and below the horizontal; however, where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
When determining the unobstructed view of the apparent surface of the rear position lamp, the illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light shall be excluded.

The electrical connections for rear position lamps shall be in accordance with paragraph 5.11, except that if a rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a direction-indicator, the electrical connection of the rear position lamp on the relevant side of the vehicle or the reciprocally incorporated part of it may be such that it is switched OFF during the entire time (both ON and OFF cycle) of operation of the direction-indicator lamp.
While daytime running lamps are not switched ON, the rear position lamp shall have a mandatory closed-circuit tell-tale.
The closed-circuit tell-tale of the rear position lamps shall be combined with that of the front position lamps; this requirement does not apply while the daytime running lamps are switched ON.
The tell-tale indicating failure of the rear position lamp shall be mandatory if required by the component Regulation.
The ESA(s) shall be tested for radiated and conducted emissions, for immunity to radiated and conducted disturbances.
The ESA representative of its type shall be tested for immunity to electromagnetic radiation such that test severity in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band are given in Table 2a.

The ESA representative of its type shall be tested for immunity to electromagnetic radiation such that test severity for the minimum test Level over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band is as given in Table 2b.

For the 24 V system starting profile (ISO 16750-2, test level II, 10 pulses), an ESA that shall be operational during engine start phases shall reach functional status class B if it performs immunity-related functions and class D if it does not, and any other ESA shall reach class C, as given in Table 3a; the starting profile applies only to ESAs that may be installed in vehicles with an internal combustion engine started by a 12 V / 24 V starter motor.

Where a vehicle or electrical/electronic system or ESA does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz, the vehicle or electrical/electronic system or ESA shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.3.2. or 6.6.2. and with Annexes 5 and 8.
In the case of front or rear position lamps, front or rear end-outline marker lamps, the arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle.
The light source module(s) shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.
The light source module(s) shall bear the specific identification code of the module where replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.

The specific identification code of the module shall comprise the starting letters “MD” for “MODULE” followed by the approval mark without the circle as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.2.1.1, in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.

Where replaceable light source module(s) is/are used and several non-identical light source modules are used, the specific identification code of the module shall be followed by additional symbols or characters.

The light source module and the lamp shall both have marks from the same applicant, where the approval mark on the light source module does not have to be the same as the one on the lamp in which the module is used, in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.
The light source module(s) shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.
The lamp shall bear the specific identification code of the module as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.3.5. (a), (ii) in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.
The lamp shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage in case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used.
The component shall have the markings in paragraphs 3.3.3.5.(a) affixed on it.

The position lamps or daytime running lamps, which are reciprocally incorporated with another function, using a common light source, and designed to operate permanently with an additional system to regulate the intensity of the light emitted, shall be permitted.

The logo light emitting surface (incorporating transparent and non-transparent components of the logo) shall not be required to be symmetrical by itself, notwithstanding the requirements of paragraph 5.5.2. of UN Regulation No. 48, when the internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside of the apparent surface of a lamp (function) incorporates only one manufacturer logo built by transparent or non-transparent components on request of the applicant.
Stop lamps, direction indicator lamps, and reversing lamps shall not incorporate a logo.

If any one light source in a single lamp containing more than one light source fails, then the single lamp shall ensure that at least one of the following provisions applies: (a) the light intensity complies with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution as shown in Annex 3 and when all light sources are illuminated the maximum intensities shall not be exceeded; or (b) a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure, as indicated in paragraphs 6.4.8., 6.7.8., 6.9.8, 6.10.8., 6.11.8., 6.12.8., 6.13.8. and 6.18.8. of UN Regulation No. 48, is produced.

The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall meet the requirements for luminous intensity and standard light distribution in Table 4, however, a luminous intensity of 6.0·10¹ cd (60 cd) shall be permitted for rear position lamps reciprocally incorporated with stop lamps below a plane forming an angle of 5° with and downward from the horizontal plane.
The light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall meet the requirements in Table 7 for luminous intensity and standard light distribution.
The measured values shall correspond to the values shown in Table 12 for the minimum values required throughout the fields specified in Annexes 2 and 3.

The luminous intensities for all other lamps (other than those mentioned in 1.2.1), measured after 1 min and either after 30 minutes of operation, or after photometric stability has occurred, shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.

The luminous intensity distribution shall, depending on the light source technology and in addition to paragraph 1, be checked for compliance at the point in time listed in Table A8-1, where the luminous intensity distributions at a point in time may be calculated from the luminous intensity distribution measured according to paragraph 1 by applying at each test point the ratio of luminous intensities measured at the reference coordinate of the lamp (function) under consideration.

extra.text: Markings on the ESA (rear combination lamp electronics) in conformity with paragraph 5.3. need not be visible when the ESA is installed in the vehicle.
The rear combination lamp ESA shall be tested for radiated emissions.
The rear combination lamp ESA shall be tested for conducted emissions.
The rear combination lamp ESA shall be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances.
The rear combination lamp ESA shall be tested for immunity to conducted disturbances.
The electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 7.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband type approval limit shall be 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 6 to this Regulation.
The electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 8.

When measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the narrowband limit in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band shall be 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 7.
For ESAs intended for vehicles with 12 V systems, the maximum allowed positive pulse amplitude of transient conducted disturbances on the supply lines shall be +75 V.
For ESAs intended for vehicles with 12 V systems, the maximum allowed negative pulse amplitude of transient conducted disturbances on the supply lines shall be -100 V.
For ESAs intended for vehicles with 24 V systems, the maximum allowed positive pulse amplitude of transient conducted disturbances on the supply lines shall be +150 V.
For ESAs intended for vehicles with 24 V systems, the maximum allowed negative pulse amplitude of transient conducted disturbances on the supply lines shall be -450 V.
When the immunity of the rear combination lamp ESA is tested by the stripline method as described in Annex 9, the test level in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 400 MHz frequency band shall be 60 V/m.
When the immunity of the rear combination lamp ESA is tested by the stripline method as described in Annex 9, the minimum test level over the whole 20 to 400 MHz frequency band shall be 50 V/m.
When the immunity of the rear combination lamp ESA is tested by the TEM cell method as described in Annex 9, the test level in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 200 MHz frequency band shall be 75 V/m.
When the immunity of the rear combination lamp ESA is tested by the TEM cell method as described in Annex 9, the minimum test level over the whole 20 to 200 MHz frequency band shall be 62,5 V/m.
When the immunity of the rear combination lamp ESA is tested by the BCI method as described in Annex 9, the test level in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 400 MHz frequency band shall be 60 mA.
When the immunity of the rear combination lamp ESA is tested by the BCI method as described in Annex 9, the minimum test level over the whole 20 to 400 MHz frequency band shall be 50 mA.
When the immunity of the rear combination lamp ESA is tested by the ALSE method as described in Annex 9, the test level in over 90 per cent of the 80 to 2,000 MHz frequency band shall be 30 V/m.
When the immunity of the rear combination lamp ESA is tested by the ALSE method as described in Annex 9, the minimum test level over the whole 80 to 2,000 MHz frequency band shall be 25 V/m.
When the immunity of the rear combination lamp ESA is tested by the ALSE method as described in Annex 9, the test level in over 90 per cent of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band shall be 10 V/m.
When the immunity of the rear combination lamp ESA is tested by the ALSE method as described in Annex 9, the minimum test level over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band shall be 8 V/m.

When the immunity of the rear combination lamp ESA is tested by the reverberation chamber method as described in Annex 9, the test level in over 90 per cent of the LUF to 2,000 MHz frequency band shall be 21 V/m.

When the immunity of the rear combination lamp ESA is tested by the reverberation chamber method as described in Annex 9, the minimum test level over the whole LUF to 2,000 MHz frequency band shall be 18 V/m.

When the immunity of the rear combination lamp ESA is tested by the reverberation chamber method as described in Annex 9, the test level in over 90 per cent of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band shall be 7 V/m.

When the immunity of the rear combination lamp ESA is tested by the reverberation chamber method as described in Annex 9, the minimum test level over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency band shall be 6 V/m.
Where the rear combination lamp ESA does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz, it shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.6.2. and with Annex 8.
ESAs with no immunity related functions need not be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.8. and with Annex 9 to this Regulation.

The conformity of production procedures for the rear combination lamp (as an electrical/electronic sub-assembly) shall comply with those set out in Schedule 1 of the 1958 Agreement (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3), with the following requirements.

The rear combination lamp as an ESA approved under UN Regulation No. 10 shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements set forth in paragraph 6. and, if applicable, in paragraph 7. of the Regulation.

Conformity of production of the rear combination lamp (component or separate technical unit) shall be checked on the basis of the data contained in the communication form(s) for type approval set out in Annex 3A and/or 3B to this Regulation.

When the conformity of an ESA taken from the series is being verified, production shall be deemed to conform to the requirements of this Regulation in relation to broadband electromagnetic disturbances and narrowband electromagnetic disturbances if the levels measured do not exceed by more than 4 dB (60 per cent) the reference limits prescribed in paragraphs 6.5.2.1., 6.6.2.1., and, if applicable, paragraph 7.10.2.1. for ESAs.

When the conformity of an ESA taken from the series is being verified, production shall be deemed to conform to the requirements of this Regulation in relation to immunity to electromagnetic radiation if the ESA does not exhibit any degradation relating to the direct control of the vehicle which could be observed by the driver or other road user when subjected to a field strength, expressed in Volts/m, up to 80 per cent of the reference limits prescribed in paragraph 6.8.2.1. and, if applicable, paragraph 7.18.2.1. for ESAs.

If the conformity of a component, or Separate Technical Unit (STU) taken from the series is being verified, production shall be deemed to conform to the requirements of this Regulation in relation to immunity to conducted disturbances if the component or STU shows no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions" up to levels given in paragraph 6.9.1. and, if applicable, paragraph 7.19.1.

If the conformity of a component, or Separate Technical Unit (STU) taken from the series is being verified, production shall be deemed to conform to the requirements of this Regulation in relation to conducted emission if the component or STU does not exceed the levels given in paragraph 6.7.1. and, if applicable, paragraph 7.17.1.

The radiated broadband electromagnetic emissions of the ESA, for a 120 kHz bandwidth, shall not exceed the limit E (dBµV/m) in the 30-75 MHz frequency band given by E = 62 - 25.13 log (F/30), where F is the frequency in MHz (see paragraphs 6.5.2.1. and 7.10.2.1. of this Regulation).

The radiated broadband electromagnetic emissions of the ESA, for a 120 kHz bandwidth, shall not exceed the limit E (dBµV/m) in the 75-400 MHz frequency band given by E = 52 + 15.13 log (F/75), where F is the frequency in MHz (see paragraphs 6.5.2.1. and 7.10.2.1. of this Regulation).

The radiated broadband electromagnetic emissions of the ESA, for a 120 kHz bandwidth, shall not exceed the limit E = 63 dBµV/m in the 400-1,000 MHz frequency band (see paragraphs 6.5.2.1. and 7.10.2.1. of this Regulation).

The narrowband electromagnetic radiation limit of the ESA (see paragraph 6.6.2.1. of this Regulation) in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band shall be E = 52 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m at frequency F (MHz) for a 120 kHz bandwidth.

The narrowband electromagnetic radiation limit of the ESA (see paragraph 6.6.2.1. of this Regulation) in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band shall be E = 42 + 15.13 log (F/75) dBµV/m at frequency F (MHz) for a 120 kHz bandwidth.
The narrowband electromagnetic radiation limit of the ESA (see paragraph 6.6.2.1. of this Regulation) in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band shall be E = 53 dBµV/m for a 120 kHz bandwidth.
For the rear combination lamp as an ESA powered by LV, a 5 µH / 50 Ω AN as defined in Figure 1 of Appendix 8 shall be used.
The AN(s) used for the rear combination lamp (ESA powered by LV) shall be mounted directly on the ground plane.
The grounding connection of the AN(s) used for the rear combination lamp (ESA powered by LV) shall be bonded to the ground plane.
Measurement ports of the AN(s) used for the rear combination lamp (ESA powered by LV) shall be terminated with a 50 Ω load.

The AN impedance ZPB (tolerance ± 20 %) in the measurement frequency range of 0,1 MHz to 100 MHz shall be as shown in Figure 2, measured between the terminals P and B (of Figure 1) with a 50 Ω load on the measurement port and with terminals A and B (of Figure 1) short circuited.
If not otherwise stated in Annex 7, the test measuring broadband electromagnetic emissions from the rear combination lamp ESA shall be performed according to CISPR 25.
The rear combination lamp ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load.

For the rear combination lamp ESA, which is not involved in "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", the test shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in Clause 6.4 of CISPR 25.

As an alternative to an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE), an open area test site (OATS) which complies with the requirements of CISPR 16-1-4 may be used for the rear combination lamp ESA test.

To ensure that there is no extraneous noise or signal of a magnitude sufficient to affect materially the measurement, ambient measurements shall be taken before or after the main test, and in this measurement the extraneous noise or signal shall be at least 6 dB below the limits of interference given in paragraph 6.5.2.1. of this Regulation, except for intentional narrowband ambient transmissions.
The broadband emission limits shall apply to the rear combination lamp ESA throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an ALSE or OATS.

If peak detectors are used for measuring the rear combination lamp ESA emissions, a correction factor of 20 dB as defined in CISPR 12 shall be applied, the limits given in paragraphs 6.5. and 7.10. of this Regulation being for quasi-peak detectors.
The measurements of the rear combination lamp ESA shall be performed with a spectrum analyser or a scanning receiver using the parameters defined in Table 1 and Table 2 of Annex 7.
If a spectrum analyser is used for peak measurements, the video bandwidth shall be at least three times the resolution bandwidth (RBW).

FFT-based measuring instruments shall continuously record and evaluate the signal during the measurement time, and the minimum measurement time shall be 1 s per analysis frequency band (in real-time mode) of the FFT instrument.
Unless otherwise specified, the configuration with the LV harness closer to the antenna shall be tested.
The phase centre of the antenna shall be in line with the centre of the longitudinal part of the wiring harnesses for frequencies up to 1,000 MHz.
In the event that the limit is exceeded during the test, investigations shall be made to ensure that this is due to the rear combination lamp ESA and not to background radiation.

The maximum of the readings relative to the limit (horizontal/vertical polarization) in each of the 14 frequency bands shall be taken as the characteristic reading at the frequency at which the measurements were made.
If not otherwise stated in Annex 8, the narrowband electromagnetic emission test of the ESA shall be performed according to CISPR 25.
The ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably in maximum load, during the radiated narrowband emission tests.
The radiated narrowband emission test of the ESA shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in paragraph 6.4. of CISPR 25.

As an alternative to an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE), an open area test site (OATS) may be used for the radiated narrowband emission test of the ESA, provided that it complies with the requirements of CISPR 16-1-4.
To ensure that there is no extraneous noise or signal of a magnitude sufficient to affect materially the measurement, ambient measurements shall be taken before or after the main test.

In the ambient measurement, the extraneous noise or signal shall be at least 6 dB below the limits of interference given in paragraph 6.6.2.1. of this Regulation, except for intentional narrowband ambient transmissions.

The narrowband emission limits for the ESA shall apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or open area test site (OATS).
The narrowband emission measurements of the ESA shall be performed with an average detector.
The narrowband emission measurements of the ESA shall be performed with a spectrum analyser or a scanning receiver, using the parameters defined in Tables 1 and 2 of Annex 8.
Spectrum analysers and FFT-based instruments may be used for conformity measurements provided that they meet the requirements of CISPR 16-1-1.
FFT-based measuring instruments shall continuously record and evaluate the signal during the measurement time.
If using FFT-based instruments, the minimum measurement time shall be 1 s per analysis frequency band (in real-time mode) of the FFT instrument.
When a spectrum analyser with average detector is used in the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz, the RBW at -3 dB shall be 100/120 kHz and the minimum scan time shall be 100 ms/MHz.
If a spectrum analyser is used for peak measurements, the video band width shall be at least three times the resolution band width (RBW).

When a scanning receiver with average detector is used in the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz, the bandwidth at -6 dB shall be 120 kHz, the maximum step size shall be 60 kHz and the minimum dwell time shall be 5 ms.

The test shall be performed at the intervals specified in the CISPR 12 standard throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz, or alternatively, if the manufacturer provides measurement data for the whole frequency band from a test laboratory accredited to the applicable parts of ISO 17025 and recognized by the Type Approval Authority, at the 14 frequencies giving the highest emission levels within each of the 14 frequency bands 30-34, 34-45, 45-60, 60-80, 80-100, 100-130, 130-170, 170-225, 225-300, 300-400, 400-525, 525-700, 700-850 and 850-1,000 MHz.
In the event that the limit is exceeded during the test, investigations shall be made to ensure that this is due to the ESA and not to background radiation including broadband radiation from the ESA.

The maximum of the readings relative to the limit (horizontal/vertical polarisation) in each of the 14 frequency bands shall be taken as the characteristic reading at the frequency at which the measurements were made.

The ESA may comply with the requirements of any combination of the following test methods at the manufacturer's discretion provided that these results in the full frequency range specified in paragraph 3.1. of Annex 9 being covered: (a) Absorber chamber test according to ISO 11452-2; (b) TEM cell testing according to ISO 11452-3; (c) Bulk current injection testing according to ISO 11452-4; (d) Stripline testing according to ISO 11452-5; (e) Reverberation chamber test according to ISO 11452-11.
The frequency range and general test conditions for the immunity tests of the ESA shall be based on ISO 11452-1.
The test conditions for the immunity testing of the ESA shall be according to ISO 11452-1.
The ESA under test shall be switched on and shall be stimulated to be in normal operation condition.
The ESA under test shall be arranged as defined in Annex 9 unless individual test methods dictate otherwise.
Any extraneous equipment required to operate the ESA under test shall not be in place during the calibration phase.
No extraneous equipment shall be closer than 1 m from the reference point during calibration.

To ensure reproducible measurement results are obtained when tests and measurements are repeated, the test signal generating equipment and its layout shall be to the same specification as that used during each appropriate calibration phase.

If the ESA under test consists of more than one unit and the wiring harnesses as intended for use in the vehicle are not available, the length between the electronic control unit and the AN shall be as defined in the standard.
The frequency step size and dwell time shall be chosen according to ISO 11452-1.
If the ESA fails the tests defined in Annex 9, it shall be verified as having failed under the relevant test conditions and not as a result of the generation of uncontrolled fields.
When the absorber chamber test is used, the "substitution method" shall be used to establish the test field conditions according to ISO 11452-2.
When the absorber chamber test is used, the test shall be performed with vertical polarization.
When TEM cell testing is used, the test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-3.

When bulk current injection testing is used, the test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-4 on a test bench with either the BCI test method with substitution method and injection probe positioned at 150 mm distance to the ESA, or the BCI test method with closed loop method and injection probe positioned at 900 mm distance to the ESA.

As an alternative the ESA may be tested while installed in the vehicle according to ISO 11451-4 with the BCI test method with substitution method and injection probe positioned at 150 mm distance to the ESA.
When stripline testing is used, the test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-5.
When the reverberation chamber test is used, the test shall be performed according to ISO 11452-11.
Unless otherwise specified, the reverberation chamber testing method shall be carried out using a test setup with ground plane.

The immunity of the rear combination lamp (ESA) to conducted transients on the vehicle power supply shall be ensured, and conducted transients from the ESA to the vehicle power supply shall be limited, using the test method of Annex 10.

The emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by ESAs on 12/24 V supply lines shall be measured according to the International Standard ISO 7637-2 on supply lines as well as on other connections of ESAs which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
The approval marking shall consist of the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
The approval marking shall consist of the symbols identifying the light signalling lamps prescribed in paragraph 3.2.4.
The approval marking shall consist of the number of this Regulation followed by the letter 'R' and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval.
The arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle in the case of rear position lamps.
If applicable, the additional letter "D" shall be placed to the right side of the symbol mentioned in paragraph 3.2.4. on lamps which may be used as part of an assembly of two independent lamps.
If applicable, the additional letter "Y" shall be placed to the right side of the symbol mentioned in paragraph 3.2.4. on lamps which are used as part of an interdependent lamps system.
On lamps with reduced light distribution, see paragraph 1.1. of Annex 3, the approval marking shall include a vertical arrow starting from a horizontal segment and directed downwards.
Lamps shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage, in the case of lamps with non-replaceable light sources.

An electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control being part of the lamp, but not included into the lamp body, shall be marked with its identification number and the name of the manufacturer.

Where grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps have been found to comply with the requirements of several UN Regulations, a single approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number may be affixed, and this marking may be located anywhere on the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, provided that it is visible after their installation.

Where a single approval mark is affixed on grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, no part of the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps that transmits light can be removed without at the same time removing the approval mark.

The conformity of production procedures for the rear combination lamp (rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions) shall comply with those set out in the 1958 Agreement, Schedule 1 (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3), with the requirements set forth in paragraph 6.
Each lamp submitted for approval (rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp) shall conform to the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4. and 5.

The requirements contained in sections 5 "General specifications" and 6 "Individual specifications" (and in the Annexes referenced in the said sections) of UN Regulation No. 48, and its series of amendments in force at the time of application for the lamp type approval, shall apply to the rear combination lamp (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and retro-reflector).

The requirements of UN Regulation No. 48 pertinent to each lamp of the rear combination lamp and to the vehicle category M1 on which the lamp is intended to be installed shall be applied, where their verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible.
An assembly of two independent lamps to be type approved as lamp marked "D" is applicable to rear position lamps.
An assembly of two independent lamps to be type approved as lamp marked "D" is applicable to stop lamps.
An interdependent lamp system to be type approved as lamps marked "Y" is applicable to rear position lamps.
An interdependent lamp system to be type approved as lamps marked "Y" is applicable to stop lamps.

Rear position lamps which are reciprocally incorporated with another function, using a common light source, and designed to operate permanently with an additional system to regulate the intensity of the light emitted, are permitted.
Stop lamps shall not incorporate a logo.
Reversing lamps shall not incorporate a logo.

In a single lamp of the rear combination lamp containing more than one light source, a group of light sources, wired so that the failure of any one of them causes all of them to stop emitting light, shall be considered to be one light source.

Reflections from the floor and walls which occur over the relatively long test distances used shall be screened from both the sample and the photometer head by baffles.

The residual stray light value measured when the sample is covered by an opaque matt black surface, zigzag folded black paper of the same size and shape or a specular black surface suitably oriented with a light trap shall be subtracted from that measured on the retro-reflective device.

In the case of moulded plastics reflectors of retro-reflecting devices of Classes IA or IB, the retro-reflective device shall be kept for 48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at a temperature of 65 °C ± 2 °C, after which the sample shall be allowed to cool for 1 hour at 23 °C ± 2 °C.

The retro-reflector, whether part of a lamp or not, shall be stripped of all removable parts and immersed for 10 minutes in water at a temperature of 50 °C ± 5 °C, the highest point of the upper part of the illuminating surface being 20 mm below the surface of the water.

The water immersion test of the retro-reflector shall be repeated after turning the retro-reflective device through 180°, so that the illuminating surface is at the bottom and the rear face is covered by about 20 mm of water.
The retro-reflector sample units shall then be immediately immersed in the same conditions in water at a temperature of 25 °C ± 5 °C.

If visual inspection does not reveal the presence of water or in case of doubt, the RI of the retro-reflector shall be measured by the method described in paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation, the retro-reflective device being first lightly shaken to remove excess water from the outside.

As an alternative, at the request of the manufacturer, the moisture and dust tests of Annex 6 Part 3 shall be applied to the retro-reflective device of Class IB or IIIB to verify resistance to water penetration.

The water spray cabinet shall be equipped with a nozzle(s) which provides a solid cone water spray of sufficient angle to completely cover the sample device, and the centreline of the nozzle(s) shall be directed downward at an angle of 45° ± 5° to the vertical axis of a rotating test platform.
The rotating test platform of the water spray cabinet shall have a minimum diameter of 140 mm and rotate about a vertical axis in the centre of the cabinet.

The precipitation rate of the water spray at the device shall be 2.5 (+1.6/-0) mm/min as measured with a vertical cylindrical collector centred on the vertical axis of the rotating test platform, with a collector height of 100 mm and an inside diameter of a minimum of 140 mm.
A sample device mounted on a test fixture, with initial RI measured and recorded, shall be subjected to the water spray test.
During the water spray test all drain holes and other openings of the device shall remain open, and drain wicks, when used, shall be tested in the device.
During the water spray test the device shall be rotated about its vertical axis at a rate of 4.0 ± 0.5 min-1.

If the retro-reflector is reciprocally incorporated or grouped with signalling or lighting functions, these functions shall be operated at design voltage according to a cycle of 5 min ON (in flashing mode, where appropriate), 55 min OFF.
The water spray test shall last 12 hours (12 cycles of 5/55 min).
After the water spray test the rotation and the water spray shall be turned OFF and the device allowed to drain for 1 hour with the cabinet door closed.

Upon completion of the drain period, the interior of the device shall be observed for moisture accumulation and no standing pool of water shall be allowed to be formed, or which can be formed by tapping or tilting the device.
After the water spray test and drain period, the RI shall be measured according to the method specified in Part 1 of Annex 4 after having dried the exterior of the device with a dry cotton cloth.

The interior of the dust exposure test chamber shall be cubical in shape in size 0.9 to 1.5 m per side, with an internal chamber volume, not including a "hopper shaped" bottom, of 2 m3 maximum, charged with 3 to 5 kg of the test dust, and the chamber shall have the capability of agitating the test dust by means of compressed air or blower fans in such a way that the dust is diffused throughout the chamber.
The test dust used shall be fine powdered cement in accordance with standard ASTM C 150-84.
A sample device, mounted on a test fixture, with the initial RI measured and recorded, shall be exposed to dust.
During the dust exposure test all drain holes and other openings of the device shall remain open, and drain wicks, when used, shall be tested in the device.
The mounted device shall be placed in the dust chamber no closer than 150 mm from a wall, and devices with a length exceeding 600 mm shall be horizontally centred in the test chamber.

The test dust shall be agitated as completely as possible by compressed air or blower(s) at intervals of 15 min for a period of 2 to 15 s for the duration of 5 hours, and the dust shall be allowed to settle between the agitation periods.

Upon completion of the dust exposure test, the exterior of the device shall be cleaned and dried with a dry cotton cloth and the RI measured according to the method specified in paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation.

The lamp, since the retro-reflective device is combined with a light, shall be stripped of all removable parts and subjected to the action of a saline mist for a period of 50 hours, comprising two periods of exposure of 24 hours each, separated by an interval of two hours during which the sample is allowed to dry.

The coefficient of retro-reflection RA of the retro-reflective areas, when measured after a recovery period of 48 hours as specified in Part 2 of Annex 6, at an entrance angle of β2 = 5° and an observation angle of α = 20', shall be not less than the value in Table 9 or more than the value in Table 10 respectively.
Before measuring the coefficient of retro-reflection after the corrosion test, the surface of the retro-reflector shall be cleaned to remove salt deposits from the saline mist.
The reverse side of the mirror-backed retro-reflective device of Class IA or IB with an accessible rear face shall be brushed with a hard nylon brush.

After having brushed, in the case of moulded plastics reflectors as Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB and IVA, the rear face of the retro-reflective device, a cotton cloth soaked in the mixture defined in Part 1 of Annex 7 shall be applied to the said rear face for one minute, after which the cotton cloth is removed and the retro-reflective device left to dry.
As soon as evaporation is completed, the reverse side of the retro-reflective device shall be brushed with the same brush as before.

The RI of the retro-reflective device shall then be measured, according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation, after the whole surface of the mirror-backed rear face has been covered with Indian ink.
The accelerated artificial weathering apparatus used for testing the retro-reflector shall be in accordance with EN ISO 4892-1:2016 and EN ISO 4892-2:2013.
The accelerated artificial weathering apparatus shall be capable to control temperature and relative humidity and shall be equipped with a water spray system.
The water spray system of the accelerated artificial weathering apparatus shall be capable to spray a minimum of 0.3 ml/cm² within 5 minutes.
The spray water used in the accelerated artificial weathering test shall be in accordance to the requirements of EN ISO 4892-2:2013.
For temperature measurement in the accelerated artificial weathering test either a Black-Standard or a Black-Panel thermometer can be used (test method TM1 and TM2).

When test method TM2 (Black-panel thermometer) is used, the retro-reflective device samples shall be exposed according to cycle No. 4 of EN ISO 4892-2:2013 with 102 min dry at a broadband (300 to 400 nm) irradiance of 60 ± 2 W/m², a narrowband (340 nm) irradiance of 0.51 ± 0.02 W/m², a black-panel temperature of 63 ± 3 °C and a relative humidity of 50 ± 10 %, followed by 18 min water spray at a broadband irradiance of 60 ± 2 W/m² and a narrowband irradiance of 0.51 ± 0.02 W/m².
Preparation of test specimens of the retro-reflective device for the accelerated artificial weathering test shall be in accordance with the general guidelines given in EN ISO 4892-2:2013.

For the resistance to fuels test, the outer surface of the retro-reflective device and, in particular, of the illuminating surface, shall be lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in a test mixture of 70 vol. per cent of n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent of toluol.

After about five minutes following the wiping with the test mixture, the outer surface of the retro-reflective device shall be inspected visually and must not show any apparent surface changes, except that slight surface cracks will not be objected to.

In the resistance to lubricating oils test for moulded plastics retro-reflectors of Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB and IVA, the outer surface of the retro-reflective device and, in particular, the illuminating surface, shall be lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in a detergent lubricating oil.

In the resistance to lubricating oils test for moulded plastics retro-reflectors of Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB and IVA, after about 5 minutes the surface of the retro-reflective device shall be cleaned.

In the resistance to lubricating oils test for moulded plastics retro-reflectors of Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB and IVA, the RI of the retro-reflective device shall then be measured according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation.
The approval marking arrangement shall be made in accordance with paragraph 3.3. of this Regulation; the arrangements in Annex 10 are given merely as examples.
The approval number of the retro-reflective device must be placed close to, but in any position in relation to, the circle surrounding the letter "E".
The digits constituting the approval number of the retro-reflective device must face the same way as the "E".
The group of symbols indicating the class of the retro-reflective device must be diametrically opposite the approval number.
It shall not be possible for the lamps of the rear combination lamp to be inadvertently maladjusted.

For the rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and retro-reflector of the rear combination lamp, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the bearing plane of the vehicle on the road, with a tolerance of ±3°.

For the rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and retro-reflector of the rear combination lamp, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ±3°.
Any specific instructions as regards fitting of the rear combination lamp laid down by the manufacturer shall be complied with.

In the absence of specific instructions, the height and orientation of the rear combination lamp (rear position, stop and reversing lamps and retro-reflector) shall be verified with the vehicle unladen and placed on a flat, horizontal surface, in the condition defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2.

In the absence of specific instructions, the lamps constituting a pair (rear position lamps, stop lamps, reversing lamps and rear retro-reflectors of the left- and right-hand rear combination lamps) shall be fitted to the vehicle symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane (this estimate to be based on the exterior geometrical form of the lamp and not on the edge of its illuminating surface referred to in paragraph 2.10.3.).

In the absence of specific instructions, the lamps constituting a pair shall be symmetrical to one another in relation to the median longitudinal plane, this requirement is not valid with regard to the interior structure of the lamp.
In the absence of specific instructions, the lamps constituting a pair shall satisfy the same colorimetric requirements.
In the absence of specific instructions, the lamps constituting a pair shall have substantially identical photometric characteristics. This shall not apply to a matched pair of a function.

On vehicles whose external shape is asymmetrical, the requirements of the preceding paragraphs on the installation of the rear combination lamps (rear position, stop and reversing lamps and retro-reflectors) shall be satisfied so far as is possible.

Where two or more lamps and/or two or more separate apparent surfaces are included into the same lamp body and/or have a common outer lens, these shall not be considered as an interdependent lamp system.

The maximum height above the ground of each lamp (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and retro-reflector) shall be measured from the highest point of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis; where the maximum height above the ground clearly meets the requirements of the Regulation, the exact edges of any surface need not be determined.

The minimum height above the ground of each lamp (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and retro-reflector) shall be measured from the lowest point of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis; where the minimum height above the ground clearly meets the requirements of the Regulation, the exact edges of any surface need not be determined.
For the purposes of reducing the geometric visibility angles, the position of a lamp with regard to height above the ground shall be measured from the H plane.

The position of the lamp, as regards width, shall be determined from that edge of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis which is the furthest from the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle when referred to the overall width; where the position, as regards width, clearly meets the requirements of the Regulation, the exact edges of any surface need not be determined.

The position of the lamp, as regards width, shall be determined from the inner edges of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis when referred to the distance between lamps; where the position, as regards width, clearly meets the requirements of the Regulation, the exact edges of any surface need not be determined.

In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface, etc.) of the stop lamp shall not be intentionally varied during the period when the stop lamp is switched ON.

In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface, etc.) of the reversing lamp shall not be intentionally varied during the period when the reversing lamp is switched ON.

The photometric characteristics of any lamp of the rear combination lamp may vary as a consequence of other lamps being switched ON or OFF, provided that any variation in the photometric characteristics is in compliance with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.

The photometric characteristics of any lamp of the rear combination lamp may vary when the lamp is being used to provide another lighting function, provided that any variation in the photometric characteristics is in compliance with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.

For the visibility of red light towards the front of a vehicle, there shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of the red rear position lamp, stop lamp or retro-reflector if viewed by an observer moving within Zone 1 in a transverse plane situated 25 m in front of the vehicle (see Annex 4).

The electrical connections shall be such that the rear position lamps, together with the front position lamps, the end-outline marker lamps, if they exist, the side-marker lamps, if they exist, and the rear registration plate lamp, can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously, except while one or more of the following conditions exist: (a) front and rear position lamps, as well as side-marker lamps when combined or reciprocally incorporated with said lamps, are switched ON as parking lamps; (b) side-marker lamps flash in conjunction with direction indicators; (c) daytime running lamps are switched ON; (d) front position lamps function is substituted under the provisions of paragraph 5.12.1.
In the case of an interdependent lamp system, all light sources of the rear position lamp shall be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.
The colour of the light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.
The colour of the light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
The colour of the light emitted by the rear position lamp shall be red.
The colour of the light reflected by the rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be red.

The number of rear position lamps, stop lamps, reversing lamps and rear retro-reflectors mounted on the vehicle shall be equal to the number indicated in the individual specifications of this Regulation.

Any lamp of the rear combination lamp (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp, retro-reflector) may be installed on movable components provided that the conditions specified in paragraphs 5.18., 5.19. and 5.20. are fulfilled.

The rear position lamps and rear retro-reflectors may be installed on movable components only if at all fixed positions of the movable components the lamps on the movable components meet all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for those lamps.

Where additional rear position lamps or rear retro-reflectors are fitted and are switched ON when the movable component is in any fixed open position, these additional lamps shall satisfy all the position, geometric visibility and photometric requirements applicable to the lamps installed on the movable component.

When the rear combination lamp (rear position, stop and reversing lamps and retro-reflector) is installed on a movable component and the movable component is in the "normal position(s) of use", the lamp shall always return to the position(s) specified by the manufacturer in accordance with this Regulation.

The apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the rear position lamps shall not be hidden more than 50 per cent by any movable component, with or without a light-signalling device installed on it, in any fixed position different from the "normal position of use", where fixed position of a movable component means the stable or natural rest position(s) of the movable component specified by the vehicle manufacturer, whether locked or not.

The apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the retro-reflectors shall not be hidden more than 50 per cent by any movable component, with or without a light-signalling device installed on it, in any fixed position different from the "normal position of use", where fixed position of a movable component means the stable or natural rest position(s) of the movable component specified by the vehicle manufacturer, whether locked or not.

If the requirement that the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the rear position lamps is not hidden more than 50 per cent by any movable component is not practicable, additional lamps satisfying all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for the rear position lamps shall be switched ON when the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of these lamps is more than 50 per cent hidden by the movable component.

If the requirement that the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the retro-reflectors is not hidden more than 50 per cent by any movable component is not practicable, additional devices satisfying all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for the retro-reflectors shall be provided for when the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the retro-reflectors is more than 50 per cent hidden by the movable component.

If the requirement that the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the rear position lamps is not hidden more than 50 per cent is not practicable and additional lamps are not used, a notice in the vehicle shall inform the user that in certain position(s) of the movable components other road users shall be warned of the presence of the vehicle on the road; for example by means of a warning triangle or other devices according to national requirements for use on the road.

With the exception of retro-reflectors, a lamp of the rear combination lamp (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp), even bearing an approval mark, is deemed not to be present when it cannot be made to operate by the sole installation of a light source and/or a fuse.

Lamps approved with light source(s) according to UN Regulation No. 37, except when such light sources are used as non-replaceable light source(s) as defined in paragraph 2.9.1.2., shall be fitted in a vehicle in such a way that the light source can be correctly replaced without the need for expert assistance and without the need for special tools, other than those provided with the vehicle by the manufacturer.

For lamps approved with light source(s) according to UN Regulation No. 37, except when such light sources are used as non-replaceable light source(s), the vehicle manufacturer shall provide with the vehicle a detailed description of the procedure for replacement.

In the case where a light source module includes a holder for an approved replaceable light source according to Regulation No. 37, this light source shall be replaceable as required in paragraph 5.23.

Any temporary fail-safe replacement of the light-signalling function of the rear position lamp is allowed, provided that the replacement function in case of a failure is similar in colour, main intensity and position to the function that has ceased to operate and provided that the replacement device remains operational in its original safety function.

During temporary replacement of the light-signalling function of the rear position lamp, a tell-tale on the dashboard (paragraph 2.3.5. of this Regulation) shall indicate occurrence of a temporary replacement and need for repair.

Rear position lamps of category R2 and stop lamps of category S2 with variable luminous intensity control, which respond simultaneously to one or more of the conditions listed in paragraphs 5.26.1. and 5.26.2., are allowed, provided that the intensity of all these lamps, when combined, grouped or reciprocally incorporated, vary all together in the same manner and in a similar proportion.

For rear position lamps of category R2 and stop lamps of category S2 with variable luminous intensity control, in the entire intensity range, the specific prescribed ratio between the luminous intensities of two lamps, if applicable, shall be maintained throughout variation transitions.

Increase and decrease of the luminous intensity of the rear position lamp of category R2 and stop lamp of category S2, in the limits prescribed in the pertinent UN Regulations, is allowed in relation to the following environmental conditions: ambient lighting, fog, snowfall, rain, spray, dust clouds, and contamination of the light emitting surface.

Independent from environmental conditions mentioned under 5.26.1., a decrease of the luminous intensity of the rear position lamp of category R2 and stop lamp of category S2, in the limits prescribed in the pertinent UN Regulations, is allowed as long as the vehicle speed is equal or less than 20 km/h or the distance to the following vehicle is equal or less than 20 m.

As long as the vehicle speed is equal or less than 50 km/h, the intensity decrease of the rear position lamp of category R2 and stop lamp of category S2 already activated under traffic conditions may remain active.
No sharp variation of intensity of the rear position lamp of category R2 and stop lamp of category S2 shall be observed during transition.

When the electrical system of the vehicle is in a constant voltage operating condition, representative for the relevant category of powered vehicle as specified by the applicant, the voltage supplied at the terminals of the rear combination lamp devices which, according to their type approval documentation, have been tested by the application of a special power supply/electronic light source control gear, or in a secondary operating mode or at a voltage requested by the applicant, shall not exceed the voltage specified for the relevant devices or functions as they have been approved, except for devices which include an electronic light source control gear, or a variable intensity control being part of the device, or only light source(s) approved according to UN Regulation No. 128.

In all cases of electric power supply conditions not covered by paragraph 5.27.1., when the electrical system of the vehicle is in a constant voltage operating condition, the voltage at the terminals of the device(s) or function(s) shall not exceed 13.5 V (12 Volt-Systems) by more than 3 per cent, except for devices which include an electronic light source control gear, or a variable intensity control being part of the device, or only light source(s) approved according to UN Regulation No. 128.

In all cases of electric power supply conditions not covered by paragraph 5.27.1., when the electrical system of the vehicle is in a constant voltage operating condition, the voltage at the terminals of the device(s) or function(s) shall not exceed 6.75 V (6 Volt-Systems) by more than 3 per cent, except for devices which include an electronic light source control gear, or a variable intensity control being part of the device, or only light source(s) approved according to UN Regulation No. 128.

In all cases of electric power supply conditions not covered by paragraph 5.27.1., when the electrical system of the vehicle is in a constant voltage operating condition, the voltage at the terminals of the device(s) or function(s) shall not exceed 28 V (24 Volt-Systems) by more than 3 per cent, except for devices which include an electronic light source control gear, or a variable intensity control being part of the device, or only light source(s) approved according to UN Regulation No. 128.
The means of controlling the maximum voltage at the terminals of the rear combination lamp may, for convenience, be located within the body of the device.
If measurements of geometric visibility are taken closer to the lamp, the direction of observation shall be shifted parallel to achieve the same accuracy.

If, when the lamp is installed, any part of the apparent surface of the lamp is hidden by any further parts of the vehicle, proof shall be furnished that the part of the lamp not hidden by obstacles still conforms to the photometric values prescribed for the approval of the device.
The LED module of the rear combination lamp (rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions) does not need to be replaceable, if so stated in the communication sheet of the component type approval.
In case of light-signalling lamps of the rear combination lamp incorporating a manufacturer logo, the lamp shall be type approved according to the requirements of the UN Regulation No. 148.
The reversing lamp shall be mandatory on motor vehicles.
On motor vehicles of category M1, one reversing lamp device shall be mandatory and a second device shall be optional.
The reversing lamp shall be positioned in height not less than 250 mm and not more than 1,200 mm above the ground.
The geometric visibility of the reversing lamp installed at the rear of the vehicle shall be defined by angle α = 15° upwards and 5° downwards, as specified in paragraph 2.10.7.

The geometric visibility of the reversing lamp installed at the rear of the vehicle shall be defined by angle β = 45° to right and to left if there is only one device, as specified in paragraph 2.10.7.

The geometric visibility of the reversing lamps installed at the rear of the vehicle shall be defined by angle β = 45° outwards and 30° inwards if there are two devices, as specified in paragraph 2.10.7.
The reversing lamp shall be oriented rearwards.
For the reversing lamp, a tell-tale indicating failure is mandatory if required by the component regulation.
Stop lamp devices of S1 or S2 categories shall be mandatory on M1 category vehicles.
The number of S1 or S2 category stop lamp devices shall be two.

For M1 category vehicles, for S1 or S2 categories stop lamp devices, that point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
S1 or S2 categories stop lamp devices shall be positioned at the rear of the vehicle.

The geometric visibility of S1 or S2 categories stop lamp devices shall have a vertical angle of 15° above and below the horizontal, except that where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
The orientation of the stop lamp shall be towards the rear of the vehicle.
The stop lamps need not function if the device, which starts and/or stops the propulsion system, is in a position that makes it impossible for the propulsion system to operate.
A tell-tale indicating failure of the stop lamp is mandatory if required by the component regulation.
The installation of rear position lamps of R or R1 or R2 categories shall be mandatory.

The number of rear position lamps shall be two, type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
There shall be no special requirement for the arrangement of the rear position lamps.
In length, the rear position lamp shall be positioned at the rear of the vehicle.

For M1 category vehicles, as an alternative to paragraph 6.10.5.1., at the discretion of the manufacturer or his duly accredited representative, and only if a rear side-marker lamp is installed on the vehicle, the geometric visibility of the rear position lamp shall have a horizontal angle of 45° outwards to 45° inwards, except that where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

For M1 category vehicles, as an alternative to paragraph 6.10.5.1., at the discretion of the manufacturer or his duly accredited representative, and only if a rear side-marker lamp is installed on the vehicle, the geometric visibility of the rear position lamp shall have a vertical angle of 15° above and below the horizontal, except that where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
The orientation of the rear position lamp shall be rearwards.
The electrical connections of the rear position lamp shall be in accordance with paragraph 5.11.
The rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be mandatory on motor vehicles.

Additional retro-reflecting devices and materials (including two retro-reflectors not complying with paragraph 6.14.4.) are permitted provided they do not impair the effectiveness of the mandatory lighting and light-signalling devices.

In height, the rear retro-reflector shall be above the ground not less than 250 mm nor more than 900 mm (not more than 1,200 mm if grouped with any rear lamp(s), 1,500 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 900 mm or 1200 mm respectively).
In length, the rear retro-reflector shall be at the rear of the vehicle.
The orientation of the rear retro-reflector shall be rearwards.
Any vehicle approved pursuant to this Regulation shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements set out in paragraphs 5. and 6. above.

For the verification of the visibility of a red lamp to the front (see paragraph 5.10.4. of this Regulation), the zones 1 and 2 explored by the eye of the observer shall be bounded in height by two horizontal planes 1 m and 2.2 m respectively above the ground.

For the verification of the visibility of a red lamp to the front (see paragraph 5.10.4. of this Regulation), the zones 1 and 2 explored by the eye of the observer shall be bounded in width by two vertical planes which, forming to the front and to the rear respectively an angle of 15° outwards from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane, pass through the point or points of contact of vertical planes parallel to the vehicle's median longitudinal plane delimiting the vehicle's overall width; if there are several points of contact, the foremost shall correspond to the forward plane and the rearmost to the rearward plane.

The position of the rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and retro-reflector, as defined in paragraph 2.1.6. of this Regulation, in width, in height and in length shall be checked in accordance with the general requirements set out in paragraphs 2.10.2., 2.10.3., 2.10.4., 2.3.3. and 5.4. of this Regulation.
The values measured for the distances of the rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and retro-reflector shall be such that the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled.
The angles of geometric visibility of the rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and retro-reflector shall be checked in accordance with paragraph 2.10.7. of this Regulation.

The values measured for the angles of geometric visibility of the rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and retro-reflector shall be such that the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled except that the limits of the angles may have an allowance corresponding to the ±3º variation permitted in paragraph 5.3. for the mounting of the light-signalling devices.
The visibility of red light from the rear position lamp, stop lamp and retro-reflector towards the front shall be checked in accordance with paragraph 5.10. of this Regulation.
The visibility of white light from the reversing lamp towards the rear shall be checked in accordance with paragraph 5.10. of this Regulation.
The electrical connections of the rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp shall be checked by switching on every lamp supplied by the electrical system of the vehicle.

The rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp and their tell-tales shall function in accordance with the provisions set out in paragraphs 5.11. to 5.14. of this Regulation and with the individual specifications applicable to each lamp.

The presence, number, colour, arrangement and, where applicable, the category of the rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and retro-reflector shall be checked by visual inspection of the lamps and their markings.

The presence, number, colour, arrangement and, where applicable, the category of the rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and retro-reflector and their markings shall be such that the requirements set out in paragraphs 5.15. and 5.16. as well as in the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled.
